authority_rule: Project remains stable while any provider binding is replaced.
Task/Execution semantics do not depend on one agent vendor.
ModelBinding can change without redefining Task or Project.
WorkspaceBinding replacement preserves project authority and reconciliation.
Release is provider-neutral and can target multiple deployment bindings.
Agent candidate completion can never directly become VERIFIED.
Reconnect, replay, workspace recovery and execution recovery remain distinct.
User can export immutable evidence for a release/execution.
Adapters are admitted only after contract/security/recovery tests.
ACP/MCP/A2A/AG-UI version profiles are conformance-tested.
A linked external account is not automatically available to every agent/project/task.
Privileged actions survive disconnect and require durable decisions.
Provider costs and execution budgets are enforced independently.
Agent capabilities are discovered and bound; no implicit feature assumptions.
Every context injection can identify source/scope and secret redaction behavior.
Delegation/handoff does not transfer more authority than the parent grant.
Different providers project into one consistent state/interaction vocabulary.
Phone can inspect/approve/cancel/recover without owning execution.
Bindings/policies/artifact lineage can be exported without exporting secrets.
External ACP/MCP/A2A clients receive scoped sessions rather than raw authority.
